study_name.evidence_quote: FMT study of metabolic syndrome patients
study_name.notes: Study name inferred from publication context; no explicit study name provided in paper.

pmid.notes: PMID derived from paper_id input; corresponds to Science 352(6285):586–589.

target_condition.evidence_quote: FMT study of metabolic syndrome patients
target_condition.notes: Primary condition explicitly stated in study description.

control.notes: Paper reports allogenic and autologous FMT groups but does not use case-control terminology compatible with schema enum. Autologous recipients serve as placebo control within study design.

body_site.evidence_quote: fecal samples from a recent FMT study
body_site.notes: Fecal samples collected at baseline and multiple post-FMT timepoints.

body_site_details.evidence_quote: transfer of a microbial community from a healthy donor to a patient
body_site_details.notes: FMT targets colonic microbiota; inferred from procedure description rather than explicitly stated for samples.

days_from_first_collection.notes: Paper reports post-FMT timepoints (2, 21, 42, 84 days) but does not provide individual sample-level days_from_first_collection values. Sample-level granularity cannot be populated without individual mapping.

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: not used antibiotics or other medication for at least 3 months before treatment
antibiotics_exclusion_period.notes: Study explicitly excluded prior antibiotic use for ≥3 months as key methodological design to minimize confounding.

dna_extraction_kit.notes: DNA extraction kit/protocol not specified in main text or visible supplementary materials provided.

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: Study sequence data reported in this paper are deposited in the European Nucleotide Archive under accession number PRJEB12357.
ncbi_accession.notes: ENA project-level accession provided for all study sequencing data.

sequencing_platform.notes: Paper states 'shotgun metagenomic' sequencing. Illumina platform inferred from EMBL Genomics Core Facility standard practices and metagenomic scale; exact platform not explicitly named in provided text.

age.notes: Participant age not reported in main text or visible supplementary materials. Table S1 reference suggests demographic data may be in supplement.

age_group.notes: Age-group classification not provided; age values required to infer.

ancestry.notes: Ancestry information not provided in main text or visible supplementary materials.

sex.notes: Participant sex not reported in main text. Table S1 may contain demographic breakdown.

country.evidence_quote: Academic Medical Center, 1105 AZ Amsterdam, Netherlands
country.notes: Study recruited from Amsterdam UMC; country inferred from institution location where study was conducted and samples collected.

location.notes: Study institution and sample collection location.

subject_id.notes: Individual participant identifiers (e.g., FMT1-5, SELF1-5) used in figures but not mapped to subject_id field in publication. Sample-level data extraction would require supplementary table cross-reference.

sample_id.notes: Sample identifiers not provided in main text. Paper states 55 fecal samples analyzed but does not assign unique sample_ids.

zigosity.notes: Twin zygosity not mentioned in paper

age_min.notes: Specific age data not provided in paper

age_max.notes: Specific age data not provided in paper

age_years.notes: Age in years not reported in paper

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: subjects in this study had not used antibiotics or other medication for at least 3 months before treatment, nor did they do so during treatment

disease.evidence_quote: fecal samples from a recent FMT study on metabolic syndrome patients
disease.notes: Applies to FMT recipients only; SELF cohort received placebo

disease_details.notes: Specific metabolic syndrome details not provided

disease_response_pfs.notes: Progression-free survival not applicable; study focused on microbiota colonization

disease_response_recist.notes: RECIST criteria not applicable; microbiota transplantation study not cancer treatment

feces_phenotype.notes: Stool phenotypes not characterized; study focused on microbial composition

fmt_id.evidence_quote: FMT 1 FMT 2 FMT 3 FMT 4 FMT 5 SELF 1 SELF 2 SELF 3 SELF 4 SELF 5
fmt_id.notes: FMT1-5 received allogenic FMT; SELF1-5 received autologous FMT (placebo)

fmt_role.evidence_quote: half of whom received a single allogenic FMT and the other half, an autologous FMT
fmt_role.notes: All participants were FMT recipients post-procedure; donor samples also collected but not characterized individually

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Neonatal data not applicable; study population not characterized by birth weight

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: Infant feeding method not applicable; adult study population

neonatal_gestational_age.notes: Gestational age not applicable; adult study population

neonatal_preterm_birth.notes: Preterm birth status not applicable; adult study population

treatment.evidence_quote: half of whom received a single allogenic FMT (from one of three lean donors) and the other half, an autologous FMT (i.e., a placebo equivalent)
treatment.notes: FMT1-5 received allogenic FMT from one of three lean donors; SELF1-5 received autologous FMT (placebo control)

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: AJCC staging not applicable; not a cancer study

tumor_staging_tnm.notes: TNM staging not applicable; not a cancer study

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: we monitored strain populations in fecal samples from a recent FMT study on metabolic syndrome patients using single-nucleotide variants in metagenomes
biomarker_name.notes: SNVs are the primary biomarkers tracked to distinguish donor and recipient strains.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: Donor-specific SNVs were most highly retained 2 days after FMT (69.3±21.8% of determinant positions)
biomarker_unit.notes: Biomarkers are quantified as percentages of determinant genomic positions.

biomarker_value.evidence_quote: Donor-specific SNVs were most highly retained 2 days after FMT (69.3±21.8%) and were still present 3 months later (37.6±16.6%)
biomarker_value.notes: Multiple measurements reported across different timepoints and categories of strain analysis.

disease_response_os.notes: This is a microbiome study on metabolic syndrome patients without disease survival outcomes reported.

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable to this study design.

ecog_performance_status.notes: Not reported in this microbiome transplantation study.

feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: We found extensive coexistence of donor and recipient strains, persisting 3 months after treatment.
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal microbiota characteristics are primary outcomes, measured through metagenomic analysis.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; this is a microbiome study without oncology outcomes.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable to this study design.

value: 10 subjects: 5 allogenic FMT recipients, 5 autologous FMT (placebo)
Three lean donors, unrelated to recipients
Samples collected pre-FMT and 4 times post-FMT
No antibiotics for ≥3 months before treatment
164 fecal metagenomes analyzed across three study groups
109 metagenomes from 48 healthy FMT-naïve individuals as control
42 species tracked at strain level across 5 phyla
Determinant positions ranged 66 to 161,800 per species (median 15,550)
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: cohort of 10 subjects—half of whom received a single allogenic FMT (from one of three lean donors) and the other half, an autologous FMT (i.e., a placebo equivalent)—had samples collected at consistent time points

host_species.evidence_quote: fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), which entails the transfer of a microbial community from a healthy donor to a patient
host_species.notes: Inferred from context describing human FMT procedure and patient cohort; standard human gut microbiota study.
